curiosities: The first models carried the PS2's own chips, so they played PS2 discs too.
Its Cell processor has a main core and eight helper cores, one switched off so more chips pass testing.
Its OtherOS option let owners install Linux, until a 2010 update took it away.
The US Air Force built a supercomputer, the Condor Cluster, from 1,760 of them.
It launched in Japan on 11 November 2006.
It came at $499 and $599 in the US.
Its Blu-ray drive helped Blu-ray win over HD DVD.
Its graphics chip, the RSX, was made by Nvidia.
The Sixaxis controller sensed motion but had no rumble; the DualShock 3 brought it back.
In 2011 the PlayStation Network was down for 23 days after an intrusion.
A Slim model came in 2009 and a Super Slim in 2012.
